Sample ballot guides

Real ballots, researched with this tool using a public building's address. Each has a neutral side-by-side comparison, plus illustrative scores for six example values profiles. AI research can be wrong: open the sources. These are not endorsements.

The tool is neutral by default; the profile table shows how values match works.

Values profiles

Six example values profiles used only by the sample guides, so readers can see how different values change the same ballot's results. Evidence is tagged once on three value tensions; each profile weighs them (1-3) and leans toward one side. These mappings are judgment calls, shown so readers can disagree.

The three value tensions:

  • U · Universalism vs. Particularism
    • + Universalism: rights and duties that extend to everyone, including people outside the community or nation (open immigration, international cooperation, universal programs)
    • - Particularism: priority for one's own nation, state or community (border enforcement, sovereignty, local control, local preference)
  • E · Equality vs. Freedom
    • + Equality: collective provision, redistribution, or rules for equity and safety (public programs, progressive taxes, regulation, worker and tenant protections)
    • - Freedom: individual choice, lower taxes, less regulation, merit-based rules, private property
  • P · Progress vs. Order and tradition
    • + Progress: changing institutions and norms toward social change and reform
    • - Order and tradition: stability, law enforcement, faith, family, cultural continuity, incremental change
